date_basis: 2026-09-24 session date; no wall-clock timestamp asserted
purpose: Measure whether a keyed choice among certified H4 wirings makes the same integral distinguisher die earlier than a fixed-AES twin. This grades one attack on two machines. It does not select a round count or a cipher.

framing.primary_claim_direction: The namespace beats the twin only if the cheapest successful integral on the candidate dies at a strictly earlier round than the same integral on the twin.
framing.equal_is_failure: Equal reach means the namespace earns nothing on this attack.
framing.hidden_wiring_is_not_the_argument: Both machines are attacked as chosen-plaintext oracles. A win that exists only because the attacker was denied the wiring schedule is out of scope; the integral does not use the schedule.
framing.absence_is_not_security: If the integral finds nothing on both machines, the search is uncalibrated unless the planted identity rotor stays balanced at every tested round.

authorization.open_choice: section 4 item 2: whether the rotor namespace earns its cost
blocked: any claim that this integral is the full attack matrix

shared.masks: 13 blocks of 32 bytes from SHAKE-256 of the domain below; identical on both machines
shared.offsets: p_in and p_out are zero. Effective masks are the shared mask schedule. The machines differ only in the row-shift tuple.

candidate.selection: round r uses catalog[SHAKE-256(domain || key_label=0 || r)[0] mod 3]

attack.balanced_means: XOR of the 256 output blocks is zero at that lane
attack.surviving_rounds: largest tested round at which all 32 lanes are balanced; 0 if round 1 is already unbalanced

planted_controls.requirement: On the candidate schedule, skipping the S-box leaves all 32 lanes balanced at every tested round. If this control is quiet, the integral is uncalibrated and no win or loss may be reported.
Repeated use of this tuple is not all-to-all by round 12. The gate must detect that before it grades the namespace.

predictions.text: The identity-rotor control stays fully balanced at every tested round.
The mono-parity wiring is detected as not all-to-all by round 12.
The win rule is applied exactly once, to the integral surviving-round counts, and equal counts are a namespace failure.
